edits.value_json: The received Shuowen entry analyzes the older “smiling appearance” use as 口 with 斤 as phonetic. A separately curated redraw depicts a 听 form associated with the Shuowen small-seal tradition, not the character’s later use for 聽. The book describes the early 聽 form as 耳 plus 口 and treats 㥁 in the seal form as an added sound marker; these are its interpretations, not direct inspection of artifact glyphs.

听 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 聽. A book account also reports that 听 has served as a simplified form of 聽 since the Yuan; the Ministry dictionary cites Song–Yuan vernacular use. These graphic correspondences do not show that the older smiling-word meaning developed into “hear” or “listen.”
Han-period literary example cited; first occurrence unresolved
听 is used as the simplified form of 聽, meaning “hear” or “listen.” Its use for 聽 is attested in Song–Yuan vernacular writing; the exact beginning and reason for this graphic reuse remain unresolved.
听 is the simplified form of 聽, meaning “hear” or “listen.” It also has a separate older use meaning “smiling appearance”; the two uses are not connected by a documented change in meaning.
